# PHP2Shell — passive checker for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619

> PHP2Shell is a free, open-source, passive checker for two critical remote-code-execution
> vulnerabilities in the PHP core: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. It reads only what a
> server discloses publicly and never exploits the flaws.

Site: https://haveibeenphpned.github.io/
Source: https://github.com/GenkaOk/haveibeenphpned
Languages: Russian (default) at `/`, English at `/en/`, French at `/fr/`
Fix guide: `/fix/` (Russian, x-default), `/en/fix/`, `/fr/fix/`
Content updated: 2026-10-23
Vulnerability fixes released: 2026-10-21

## What the vulnerabilities are

CVE-2026-109618 — incorrect state after an out-of-memory error.
A failure while handling an out-of-memory condition leaves the PHP core in an incorrect state
that can let an attacker take control of the process (remote code execution).

CVE-2026-109619 — stale PHP-FPM worker state between requests.
A PHP-FPM worker reuses state from a previous request, which can affect how the next request is
handled and lead to remote code execution.

Both CVEs have severity 9.2 (critical) and affect the PHP core itself, not a framework or an
application. The same fixed versions address both.

## Affected branches and fixed versions

| PHP branch | Fixed version | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8.5 | 8.5.12 | fixed |
| 8.4 | 8.4.27 | fixed |
| 8.3 | 8.3.36 | fixed |
| 8.2 | 8.2.35 | fixed |
| 8.1, 8.0, 7.x, 5.x | — | no upstream release; distribution/Sury backports may exist |

A version below the fixed release for its branch remains vulnerable. Versions at or above the
fixed release are not vulnerable to these two CVEs.

## If you are stuck on PHP 8.1, 8.0 or 7.x

No upstream PHP release fixes these branches. A backport may still be available from the
distribution or from deb.sury.org. Check the package version, not only the version reported by
`X-Powered-By`.

Verified on 2026-10-23:

| Distribution | Package | Fixed version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Debian 12 bookworm | php8.2 | 8.2.35-1~deb12u1 |
| Debian 13 trixie | php8.4 | 8.4.27-1~deb13u1 |
| Ubuntu 22.04 LTS | php8.1 | 8.1.2-1ubuntu2.28 |
| Ubuntu 24.04 LTS | php8.3 | 8.3.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.13 |
| Ubuntu 26.04 / 26.10 | php8.5 | 8.5.4-0ubuntu1.5 / 8.5.9-0ubuntu2.1 |

deb.sury.org rebuilt php8.1 8.1.34-9, php8.0 8.0.30-25, php7.4 7.4.33-31, php7.3 7.3.33-35,
php7.2 7.2.34-66, php7.1 7.1.33-81, php7.0 7.0.33-93 and php5.6 5.6.40-105 on 2026-10-21/22.
Their `debian/changelog` contains `Backported from 8.2.35: [CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619]`.
Sury is a third-party repository, not the official Debian/Ubuntu security channel: take a backup,
test on staging, and read the changelog of the exact package.

Debian Security Tracker: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-109618
and https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-109619
Ubuntu USN-8948-1: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8948-1
Sury repository and setup: https://packages.sury.org/php/ (README.txt)
Sury changelog example: https://packages.sury.org/php/pool/main/p/php8.1/php8.1_8.1.34-9+0~20261021.82+debian12~1.gbp4e430a.debian.tar.xz

## How the check works

1. The checker makes one or two ordinary GET or HEAD requests to the site root. Redirects are
   followed within a small fixed budget.
2. It reads only public data: the `Server`, `X-Powered-By` and `Set-Cookie` headers and PHP
   markers in the response body.
3. It compares the disclosed PHP version with the fixed release for that branch.
4. It returns a verdict for each CVE with the evidence it used.

The check is passive: it does not run the vulnerable code, does not change server state, and
does not scan ports, paths, wordlists or parameters. It is not a penetration test and it does
not prove that a server is exploitable.

## Verdicts

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `vulnerable` | The disclosed PHP version is below the fixed release for both CVEs or for one of them. |
| `likely_vulnerable` | The version belongs to an affected branch, but the exact patch level cannot be confirmed. |
| `not_vulnerable` | The disclosed version is at or above the fixed release — no update is needed. |
| `not_applicable` | No PHP signs were found — these CVEs do not apply to the server. |
| `unknown` | The PHP version could not be determined; a manual audit is needed. |

Distribution builds often backport patches into older version numbers, so a disclosed version
can be vulnerable or fixed independently of the upstream number. Doubtful cases need manual
verification on the server.

## API

The browser UI uses a small JSON API. Both endpoints are CORS-restricted to the site's own
origins and rate-limited to 10 checks per minute per IP.

### GET /api/health

```json
{ "ok": true }
```

### POST /api/check

Request body:

```json
{ "url": "https://example.com", "lang": "en", "deep": false }
```

`lang` is optional (`ru`, `en` or `fr`) and only affects human-readable strings. `deep` is
optional and defaults to `false`; any value other than `true` keeps the passive mode.

Example request:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://<api-host>/api/check" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url":"https://example.com","lang":"en"}'
```

Response (shortened):

```json
{
  "target": "https://example.com",
  "finalUrl": "https://example.com/",
  "scannedAt": "2026-10-22T12:00:00.000Z",
  "summary": {
    "status": "vulnerable",
    "label": "vulnerable",
    "counts": { "vulnerable": 2, "likely_vulnerable": 0, "not_vulnerable": 0,
                "not_applicable": 0, "unknown": 0 }
  },
  "php": { "detected": true, "version": "8.4.26", "versionSource": "header" },
  "cves": [
    { "id": "CVE-2026-109618", "severity": 9.2, "status": "vulnerable",
      "advisory": "https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w" }
  ],
  "recommendations": ["Update PHP to the fixed release for your branch"],
  "disclaimer": "Passive check; the vulnerability is not exploited."
}
```

Errors: `400` invalid URL or body, `403` target blocked by the SSRF guard, `415` body is not
JSON, `429` rate limit (with `Retry-After`), `500` internal error.

## Limitations

- The verdict depends on what the server discloses. If the PHP version is hidden, the result is
  `unknown`.
- Reverse proxies, CDNs and custom `Server` headers can hide or distort the PHP version.
- Linux distribution backports can make a disclosed version number unreliable.
- Only these two CVEs are checked; the tool is not a general vulnerability scanner.
- The check says nothing about whether a server is already compromised.

## Privacy

- No account, no cookies for tracking, no database of checked addresses.
- The API log records only the HTTP method and path of the API request, not the target URL.
- The report is returned to the browser and is not stored server-side.

## How to cite this site

Suggested citation:

> PHP2Shell. (2026). Passive checker for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.
> https://haveibeenphpned.github.io/ (accessed 2026-10-23).

In running text, prefer: "PHP2Shell, a free passive checker for CVE-2026-109618 and
CVE-2026-109619 (https://haveibeenphpned.github.io/)". When quoting the fixed versions, cite
PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, released on 2026-10-21.
